behavioral_requirements.validation_scope: Documented algorithm requirements only. The cases array above contains executable decoder rejection fixtures. These requirements and behavioral_scenarios below are not JSON-decoder conformance tests and do not demonstrate runner or queue correctness.

result_classes.same_operation_submit: Replay while retained. After eviction or restart, recover committed from the receipt scan; decide already_satisfied or conflict again.
result_classes.binding: May release or start a new operation after already_satisfied or conflict; committed satisfies assignment.

result_classes.same_operation_submit: Run again; do not replay the cached failure. Skip the seal check but adopt a committed receipt when CP is readable.
result_classes.binding: Keep target and operation ID; retry the same request bytes.
result_classes.guarantee: Only no commit seen at the closing scan, if one ran.

results: Every other rejected or unavailable result
result_classes.same_operation_submit: Run again; do not replay the cached failure.
result_classes.binding: May release or start a new operation; contention requires a new operation.
result_classes.guarantee: Return only with a seal: no membership/create attempt of this request from any process has committed or can commit. reg/ver may have committed.

result_classes.same_operation_submit: Join an active run for at most wait_ms; a sealing operation runs again.

required: Closing scan reads witness version V_c, then receipts through first absent index n*.
No child sent by this process for this operation is unresolved.
At least one of S1, S2 or S3 holds.
seal.S1: n* exceeds the first absent index on this process's first scan of the operation, or no index is absent.
seal.S2: V_c > V_epoch from this process's first fresh gateway read.
seal.S3: set_primary only: this process has seen this operation's reg-1 absent by verified not_found; the closing scan reads it when needed.
seal.unproven: Return reconciling(membership_effect_unknown|create_effect_unknown) according to operation kind, with poll_after_ms 30000.
seal.phase: Every 30 seconds rerun only closing scan and seal check, without a new attempt. Adopt committed, or return the already-decided failure when sealed. Retain as open without the R8 thread lock.
seal.R8: New process first reads CP only after prior process exits. Overlap preserves at-most-one state-changing commit per operation but voids seals.
seal.children: Record unresolved before send. First-absent allocation also applies to reg/ver; their receipts never finish the operation. Send mem only while holding this operation's reg receipt.

behavioral_requirements.retention_and_read: Keep finished results 24 hours, at most the newest 1,000; keep open/sealing until finished. Read memory only: latest run or null. A retained failure describes only its closing scan; only submit refreshes it.
behavioral_requirements.settled_guarantee: committed is final and sticky. For already_satisfied and conflict, no membership/create attempt of this request from any process has committed or can; reg/ver may have committed. The INV-6-prime proof is over actions possible for this request, with E <= V under R8 and V-prime = V.
behavioral_requirements.queue_binding: Bind target thread, operation ID and identical request bytes rebuilt from sealed intent. Change binding only after settled/sealed; raise attempt only for operation n+1. Fence request and thread until then. Owner cancel stops submits and releases fence; a late commit stands, and reuse requires a new expected-unassigned operation.
behavioral_requirements.inline_create: Keep operation ID per (registry, name) until settled or sealed.

behavioral_scenarios.name: exited-process-gap-is-sealing
behavioral_scenarios.verification: Documented behavioral scenario; requires a scripted fake CP and queue harness, not a JSON decoder.
behavioral_scenarios.setup: A has mem-1 attach at version V held in flight, then exits. B sees reg-1 present, a quiet registry and pending verification.
steps: Run B and inspect the queue binding.
Release mem-1 and resubmit the same operation.
expected: B returns reconciling, not unavailable; queue keeps its binding.
Next resubmit returns committed; exactly one membership exists and queue attempt is unchanged.

behavioral_scenarios.name: sealed-failure-does-not-trap-cache
behavioral_scenarios.verification: Documented behavioral scenario; requires a scripted fake CP and runner harness, not a JSON decoder.
behavioral_scenarios.setup: A fresh operation returns sealed unavailable(verification_pending) through S3.
steps: Resubmit the same operation after verification can succeed.
Resubmit again while committed is retained.
Evict the retained result, restart and resubmit.
expected: The first retry runs again and commits.
The next retry replays committed with zero CP calls.
After eviction and restart, the receipt scan returns committed.

behavioral_scenarios.name: request-specific-inv-6-prime
behavioral_scenarios.verification: Documented behavioral property and interleaving; requires a loopback CP/planner harness, not a JSON decoder.
behavioral_scenarios.setup: Enumerate every combination of expected, target, membership state and Acts(request). Acts includes attach/reattach for expected unassigned or any, plus move/remove from the expected source or any source for expected any.
steps: Check CP preconditions for each possible action whenever the planner returns conflict or already_satisfied, with E <= V and V-prime = V.
Hold queue attach(G) at E = V in flight; return conflict, release the slot, then deliver the late attach.
expected: Every action possible for that request fails its CP preconditions in those decision states: attach/reattach need no open primary, remove needs its observed membership open, move needs it an open primary.
Conflict permits slot release; late attach receives membership_conflict.

behavioral_scenarios.name: queue-retry-table-preserves-binding
behavioral_scenarios.verification: Documented behavioral scenario; requires a queue harness and scripted operation responses, not a JSON decoder.
behavioral_scenarios.setup: A queue has a durable binding with target, operation ID and request bytes reconstructed from sealed intent.
steps: Return CONFIG offline, reconciling and HTTP 404 in separate runs.
Return sealed thread_not_found for a flexible slot, then contention in a separate run.
Restart the queue and retry an unresolved binding.
expected: CONFIG offline, reconciling and 404 never release, reselect or increment attempt.
thread_not_found selects another slot; contention backs off and starts operation n+1.
Restart resubmits identical bytes with the same operation ID.

behavioral_scenarios.name: leave-sealing-on-registry-write-and-retry-config-create
behavioral_scenarios.verification: Documented behavioral scenarios; require a scripted fake CP, runner and controlled clock, not a JSON decoder.
behavioral_scenarios.setup: An exited process leaves an operation that cannot yet be sealed. Separately, create is denied permission.
steps: Keep the registry quiet, then commit an unrelated registry write and run the 30-second seal check.
Run create with permission_denied, fix permission, then retry the same operation.
expected: The first operation remains reconciling until the unrelated write; the 30-second check returns the decided failure without a submit.
Create returns CONFIG permission_denied immediately; retry after the fix creates exactly one workstream.
